dedupe_keys.name: building damage model validation data for hurricane michael 2018 at mexico beach florida hazus mh hindcast

description: This DesignSafe dataset supports a model-to-data validation of the HAZUS-MH hurricane damage model, comparing predicted and observed structural damage to buildings in Mexico Beach, Florida, which Hurricane Michael struck in 2018. It was published in 2026 by Mehrshad Amini, Daniel Cox, Jaimlyn Sypniewski, Omar Nofal, John van de Lindt and Trung Do. It holds inputs and results for HAZUS-MH Level 1 analyses, using the generalised national database, and Level 2 analyses, with user-defined hazard data and building inventory, for a hindcast of the storm. Observations come from independent field surveys by the StEER network and virtual damage assessment by Colorado State University and Oregon State University, with a quality-assurance procedure that examines uncertainty in first-floor elevation and damage states. Coverage is the town of Mexico Beach. Access: open download from DesignSafe with DOI 10.17603/ds2-771v-9v84. Licence: Open Data Commons Attribution; free. Caveats: one town and one storm; HAZUS itself is needed to rerun the analyses. Simulation uses are validating and calibrating wind and surge damage models, and showing the gain from local inventory and hazard data. Related records: StEER reconnaissance reports and the empirical hurricane fragility curves.
